cohort: Singleton pregnancies > 20 weeks' gestation in South Australia (n=407,580)
finding: This study found that kidney disorders during pregnancy were associated with increased risk of adverse obstetric and perinatal outcomes, with the specific risks varying depending on the type of kidney disorder.
mod_finding: Women with a history of kidney disorders had an increased risk of Cesarean section, including Cesarean section without labor, compared to women without kidney disorders.
